s: Self-managed HTTP server (nginx-style) that accepts traffic, terminates TLS, and forwards to upstream pools - cheap, fast, fully under your control.
w: The proxy maintains persistent upstream connection pools so backends avoid TCP setup cost, offloads TLS decryption, serves static files directly from disk/cache, compresses responses, and load-balances across registered upstreams with round-robin or least-connections. Config is declarative files reloaded atomically (no downtime).
use: Terminating TLS in your own VPC instead of paying managed-gateway prices
Serving static assets or SPA bundles directly alongside API proxying
Fronting a small fleet (2-20 instances) where a full API gateway is overkill
Blue-green deploys by switching an upstream block between old/new target groups
Adding gzip/brotli compression and HTTP caching headers uniformly
avoid: Deep per-client authentication and quota enforcement (that is api_gateway territory)
Teams without ops capacity to patch/config-test it - managed gateways shift that burden

size.rps_per_instance: ~30k rps per instance depending on payload sizes; CPU-bound on TLS

world: Envoy in front of Lyft's services

pat.d: An envoy/nginx sidecar next to every pod gives each service local TLS/retry logic.

pits: File-descriptor exhaustion under connection storms - raise worker_connections and enable reuseport
Config syntax errors on reload - always run nginx -t in CI and on deploy hooks
tips: Contrast with api_gateway: proxy = transport concerns, gateway = product/API concerns
Mention connection pooling benefit for chatty internal RPC
